core.title: Point every documentation relationship at a declared document id
core.given: An authored documentation corpus whose documents carry relationship attributes that name other documents by their declared ids.
core.when: You add or change a relationship attribute, edit a document that carries one, or delete a document or change a declared document id that other documents may name.
core.then: Every relationship attribute MUST name a document id that some document in the corpus actually declares.
prefer: Either declare the target, or fix the reference: a misspelled or otherwise undeclared target id is REPORTED, never silently resolved.
If the target does not exist yet, the reference is premature. Author the target document first.
Use only the four shipped relationship verbs: decides, supersedes, implements, depends-on.
avoid: Edges to a document you only intend to write. To every reader and every tool, they look the same as edges to a deleted document.
The `refines` verb. It is deliberately not shipped (spec 2 §9 Decision 3).
unless: An absent attribute is not an unresolved edge. Only declared relationships are resolved.
core.why: Resolve or report, never invent. A target outside the declared-id set is a REPORTED finding, never a synthesized node. This is the one hard requirement of spec 2 §5.4.
evidence: A corpus-wide resolution of the whole documentation corpus: every relationship target is in the declared-id set, and there are zero unresolved-target findings.
verification: A repository-wide check builds the declared-id set — the identifiers the authored corpus itself declares — BEFORE any edge is resolved, then admits a relationship only if its target is in that set; every other edge is an unresolved-target finding. The set is closed and enumerable, which is why the documentation graph can hold a discipline the traceability graph does not.
Only declared relationships are resolved: an absent attribute is not an unresolved edge and produces no finding.
Only the four shipped relationship verbs are recognized; `refines` is not among them and is not resolved.

Strict disposition, severity 1: every unresolved-target finding fails the check; there is no advisory mode, and nothing is exempt from the no-fabrication half — no configuration permits synthesizing a node for an undeclared target.
The concrete resolver and finding ids are realization details; each stack provides its own corpus-wide resolver, and the check covers the whole documentation corpus.

fires: A relationship attribute names an id that no document in the corpus declares (for example a typo).
A relationship points at a document that has not been written yet.
A document is deleted, or its declared id is changed, while other documents still name the old id.
An edit to a document that still carries an unresolved relationship attribute.
doesNotFire: A document has no relationship attributes. An absent attribute is not an unresolved edge.
Work on the resolver's own design or code. The resolver parts cover that work, and they are delivered with this part through `requires`.

profileRequirements.meaning: The file kind (and its suffix/name pattern) of the authored documentation corpus from which the documentation graph is derived; the core's file_kind activation fact and the check's scan scope are expressed through it.
How an authored documentation document declares its own identifier; the declared-id set that every relationship target must resolve against is read from these declarations.

The syntax by which an authored documentation document declares a relationship to another document by its declared id. The verb set itself (decides, supersedes, implements, depends-on) is convention-defined and stays in the core; only the attribute syntax comes from the profile.

bunOnly.text: `:implements: purpose.worktrees` resolves, while `purpose.wortrees` (a typo) is REPORTED.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete AsciiDoc reference example (the stack's attribute syntax plus example doc-ids); the core keeps a neutral counterpart and bun.json itself remains the worked reference example for other stacks.

bunOnly.text: Run the docs_capability resolver over the whole corpus.
bunOnly.reason: docs_capability is this rule's Bun validator id; the core's evidence and verification name the check generically (a corpus-wide resolution of every relationship target against the declared-id set).

bunOnly.text: Emitted by the docs_capability resolver over the whole corpus.
bunOnly.reason: Names the Bun validator that emits the finding; the core keeps the neutral finding kind and its needs_new_observer observability, while the emitter id is a realization detail.

neutralityNotes: The core speaks of an authored documentation corpus, declared document ids and relationship attributes; the concrete file kind (adoc), the id-declaration syntax (`:doc-id:`) and the relationship-attribute syntax (`:decides:`/`:supersedes:`/`:implements:`/`:depends-on:`) come from the profile (suffix.documentation plus the idiom.docs_syntax map entries doc_id_declaration and doc_relationship). suffix.documentation is the closed vocabulary's existing documentation file-kind key and matches the authored documentation corpus exactly (AsciiDoc is the stack's authored documentation format); no separate or additional file-kind key is needed. The four-verb set and the `refines` exclusion are convention semantics (spec 2 §5.2, §9 Decision 3) and therefore stay in the core, since a stack change alters only how a relationship is spelled, not which verbs exist. The validator id (docs_capability), its finding id and the concrete typo example are realization details kept in bunOnly; severity and disposition (strict, severity 1) are rule facts carried in core:verification.
